messages.body_plain:
Antje,

could you by any chance send me the code you're using to reproduce the issue? This could be a bug somewhere but it's hard to tell until I can reproduce it.  Also do I assume correctly that you're using Rserve? REngine can be used with different back-ends. If you do, then please make sure you test the latest version (1.8-1) since they have been several bugfixes related to memory management.

Thanks,
Simon

messages.subject: Help with Rserver instances locked
messages.body_plain:
Hi guys, I'm facing a weird problem and looking for some help.

I have a ruby client talking to Rserve, and sometimes (randomly, once or
twice in a day) the connection raise a Timeout exception, and from that
moment all the commands passed to Rserve are not responding.

I have to manually restart the app, so it re-connects with Rserve.

Do you know where do I have to look? I'm very blind, there's no logs
indicating the problem.

Thanks a lot!
Francisco

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

My java function returned a string which was abcd\0efg  and returned
it to R encoded as

abcd\xc0\x80efg

Could you point me to the source file where the string handling from
java to R happens?

Thanks in advance
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: How does rJava encode strings with \0 in them
messages.subject_clean: How does rJava encode strings with \0 in them
messages.body_plain:
On Mar 30, 2015, at 8:03 PM, Saptarshi Guha <saptarshi.guha at gmail.com> wrote:

> Hello,
> 
> My java function returned a string which was abcd\0efg  and returned
> it to R encoded as
> 
> abcd\xc0\x80efg
> 
> Could you point me to the source file where the string handling from
> java to R happens?
> 

It is simply using JNI GetStringUTFChars() which yields "modified UTF-8" which encodes NUL in 2-byte (11-bit) UTF-8 form. Since R doesn't support embedded NULs it's an interesting solution.

Cheers,
Simon



> Thanks in advance
> Saptarshi
